topic.reason: Forschungsergebnisse zu KI und Sprachmodellen (Treffer: we propose, memory, agent)

entries.summary: Scaling the horizon of agentic LLMs is bottlenecked by the need to fit ever longer context traces in GPU memory. Context compaction has been the most popular mechanism to alleviate this issue, keeping GPU memory constant for a given trace. Unfortunately, most compaction strategies rely on prefilling the LLM context many times over, hindering training throughput. To alleviate this bottleneck and enable efficient trainable compaction, we propose KV-streams, a plug-and-play strategy compatible with any compaction strategy that substantially increases throughput while showing no evidence of hindering performance. KV-streams enable scalable compaction by streaming the KV cache forward rather than flushing it after each compaction. topic.reason: Forschungsergebnisse zu KI und Sprachmodellen (Treffer: we propose, this paper, agent)

entries.summary: Socially intelligent language agents must negotiate, coordinate, and resolve conflicting preferences while respecting the time and attention of both participants. Balancing these demands is challenging because agents must convey enough to address a partner's constraints and advance their goals without adding words that do not help the interaction. In this paper, we propose Teacher-Assisted Communication Training (TACT) to improve social goal attainment while reducing communication cost, making interactions with agents more productive and less demanding. We first characterize communication efficiency in terms of action strategy and expression, whose effects extend beyond the current utterance to the partner's response and subsequent exchanges. We design TACT to revise student-generated actions, test the revisions through partner responses, and distill useful feedback into the student. An expression specialist removes unnecessary detail while preserving the intended action, while a strategy specialist proposes alternatives that may better address the partner's constraints. entries.title: Improving Test-Time Scaling with Adaptive Looped Transformers

topic.reason: Neue KI-Modelle, Funktionen, Benchmarks (Treffer: model, benchmark)

entries.summary: Looped transformers have demonstrated promising parameter efficiency by reusing layers for latent computation. Prior studies compare looped and non-looped models at matched parameters or per-token FLOPs. However, to the best of our knowledge, whether looping improves test-time scaling as outputs grow longer remains underexplored. Through post-training looped transformers, we study the accuracy-compute slope, measured as the accuracy gain per doubling of test-time decoding FLOPs. We find that existing looped transformers often yield steeper slopes than their non-looped baseline, yet underperform it at matched compute. While fixed-depth looping spends extra iterations on every token, our analysis shows that many tokens do not benefit from extra iterations. We therefore propose TaH2, which enables the model to focus extra iterations on the tokens that benefit from looping. It jointly post-trains the backbone and an iteration decider through lookahead depth supervision, which uses online labels indicating whether further iteration improves the prediction. entries.summary: Offizielle Release-Notes (v0.34.1): ## What's Changed * MLX safetensors `ollama create` no longer experimental. GGUF model creation now requires using llama.cpp tooling for safetensor conversion and quantization. * Improved MLX memory handling on Apple Silicon * Runaway repeat token detection now requires 100 repeat tokens for reduced false positives (e.g. OCR) * `/api/tags` is much faster on large model libraries (3.1 s → 294 ms cold in testing), and model capabilities are now reported consistently. * Deprecated `typical_p`: it can no longer be set when creating new models, existing GGUF models retain support. * MLX and llama.cpp updates **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.34.0...v0.34.1-rc1

entries.summary: Offizielle Release-Notes (v0.34.3): ## What's Changed `GET /api/show` now advertises each model's thinking controls and default: Available in the CLI with: ``` ollama show gemma4 ``` ``` thinking levels false, true default true ``` Available in the API with: ```sh curl http://localhost:11434/api/show -d '{"model": "glm-5.3-flash:cloud"}' ``` ```json { "thinking": { "values": ["low", "high", "max"], "default": "max" } } ``` Also available on ollama.com directly for cloud models. * **Nemotron H** vision models are now supported on Apple Silicon with MLX * Ollama's macOS app will now no longer reopen windows you've closed when activating it * Fix for model pulls from HuggingFace **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.34.2...v0.34.3

current.summary:
Offizielle Release-Notes (b11114): server: fix router eviction races with the existing queue (#29217) * server: route every model load through the queue A model loaded by the fast path has no queue entry, so tick() evicts
it at its LOADED transition before its own request is proxied. Every
load now joins the queue, whose entry protects the model until its
waiters leave. * server: do not admit requests into a stopping model A request for a model that is being stopped still sees it LOADED and
is proxied into the dying child. Such a request now joins the queue
and is served by the next instance. The stopping mark is cleared
under the same lock that sets UNLOADED, so no request can see a
model that is neither stopping nor unloaded while its child is gone. **Website:**
- **Attestations:**
- **macOS/iOS:**
- [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11114/llama-b11114-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz)
- macOS Apple Silicon (arm64, KleidiAI enabled) [DISABLED](https://github.com/ggml-org/llam

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11190): mtmd: fix mel preprocessor in LFM2 audio (#29403) which resulted in different greedy transcripts for 4.5% of English and 6.5% of Japanese
test utterances. In Japanese, some differences changed entire words. This change: * uses `log(x + 2^-24)` instead of clamping to the log floor
* uses a symmetric Hann window, equivalent to `torch.hann_window(periodic=False)`
* adds the normalization epsilon to the standard deviation instead of inside the square root Only the `lfm2a` preprocessor opts into these behaviors. Other audio preprocessors are unchanged. Tested on top of 84e76d8 using `llama-server` with CUDA and `temperature=0`, compared against
http://github.com/Liquid4All/liquid-audio fp32. Test set: * 200 LibriSpeech `test-clean` utterances (EN)
* 200 Common Voice `ja` test utterances (JP)
* identical 16 kHz audio passed to both implementations | Greedy transcript identical to `liquid-audio` | Without fix | With fix |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------: | -------

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11184): metal: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (#29095) * metal: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 The Metal FWHT covers widths 64 to 512, one row per simdgroup with N/32 values
per lane. Wider blocks need more registers per lane than that layout allows. kernel_fwht_tg runs one row per threadgroup with 256 threads, so each thread
keeps N/256 values. Butterflies below the simdgroup width still shuffle, those
up to the threadgroup width go through threadgroup memory, and the rest stay in
registers. Same butterfly and sign convention as the simdgroup kernel. Widths 64 to 512 keep the simdgroup kernel. 1024 through 8192 use the new one,
for both F32 and F16 sources. The wide kernels allocate float[N] of threadgroup memory, 32 KB at 8192, so the
size check takes the device limit and reports those widths as unsupported where
they would not fit. Without that a device with less threadgroup memory would
accept the op and then abort on a nil pipeline. test-backend-ops on M5 Pro: MUL_MAT_HA

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11190): mtmd: fix mel preprocessor in LFM2 audio (#29403) which resulted in different greedy transcripts for 4.5% of English and 6.5% of Japanese
test utterances. In Japanese, some differences changed entire words. This change: * uses `log(x + 2^-24)` instead of clamping to the log floor
* uses a symmetric Hann window, equivalent to `torch.hann_window(periodic=False)`
* adds the normalization epsilon to the standard deviation instead of inside the square root Only the `lfm2a` preprocessor opts into these behaviors. Other audio preprocessors are unchanged. Tested on top of 84e76d8 using `llama-server` with CUDA and `temperature=0`, compared against
http://github.com/Liquid4All/liquid-audio fp32. Test set: * 200 LibriSpeech `test-clean` utterances (EN)
* 200 Common Voice `ja` test utterances (JP)
* identical 16 kHz audio passed to both implementations | Greedy transcript identical to `liquid-audio` | Without fix | With fix |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------: | -------

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11184): metal: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (#29095) * metal: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 The Metal FWHT covers widths 64 to 512, one row per simdgroup with N/32 values
per lane. Wider blocks need more registers per lane than that layout allows. kernel_fwht_tg runs one row per threadgroup with 256 threads, so each thread
keeps N/256 values. Butterflies below the simdgroup width still shuffle, those
up to the threadgroup width go through threadgroup memory, and the rest stay in
registers. Same butterfly and sign convention as the simdgroup kernel. Widths 64 to 512 keep the simdgroup kernel. 1024 through 8192 use the new one,
for both F32 and F16 sources. The wide kernels allocate float[N] of threadgroup memory, 32 KB at 8192, so the
size check takes the device limit and reports those widths as unsupported where
they would not fit. Without that a device with less threadgroup memory would
accept the op and then abort on a nil pipeline. test-backend-ops on M5 Pro: MUL_MAT_HA

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11216): sycl: FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (#29243) The SYCL FWHT covers 64 to 512 via the standard butterfly network, plus
384/640/768/1280 via the Kronecker/Paley construction added separately in
Hadamard hint can produce (1024, 2048, 4096, 8192); those still fall through
to the default case and run as a dense GEMM against the materialized
rotation tensor, correct but O(n^2) instead of O(n log n). fwht_kernel_wide runs one row per work-group instead of per sub-group, so
each work-item keeps N/NT values rather than N/WARP_SIZE. Butterflies below
the sub-group width still shuffle; those up to the work-group width go
through work-group local memory; the rest stay in registers. Same butterfly
and sign convention as the existing narrow kernel. ggml's SYCL backend registration (dpct::dev_mgr) unconditionally requires a
GPU-labeled platform to exist and throws before any op-level test can run,
so test-backend-ops could not be exercised on this box (a GPU-less pod) even
via the CPU device

current.summary: Offizielle Release-Notes (b11227): context : do not re-reserve the scheduler when toggling causal_attn (#28751) * context : do not re-reserve the scheduler when toggling causal_attn `llama_context::set_causal_attn()` marks the scheduler to do a full re-reserve on every change of the flag. For vision inputs, this flag is flipped twice around each non-causal image chunk for Gemma models, resulting in two expensive `sched_reserve()` passes per image. This is especially slow for multi-image or video inputs. The cost of a re-reserve scales with context and ubatch configurations, so larger settings pay more per image (see table below). The re-reserve is unnecessary in this case because `causal_attn` only changes the values written to KQ mask, not tensor shapes or any other buffer sizes. Note: `causal_attn` is a graph reuse key (`llm_graph_params` via `cparams`), so a new graph is built regardless of `sched_need_reserve`, so this doesn't change the graph rebuilding behaviour. llama-server with gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_0 + BF16 mmpro

current.summary: Offizielle Release-Notes (b11227): context : do not re-reserve the scheduler when toggling causal_attn (#28751) * context : do not re-reserve the scheduler when toggling causal_attn `llama_context::set_causal_attn()` marks the scheduler to do a full re-reserve on every change of the flag. For vision inputs, this flag is flipped twice around each non-causal image chunk for Gemma models, resulting in two expensive `sched_reserve()` passes per image. This is especially slow for multi-image or video inputs. The cost of a re-reserve scales with context and ubatch configurations, so larger settings pay more per image (see table below). The re-reserve is unnecessary in this case because `causal_attn` only changes the values written to KQ mask, not tensor shapes or any other buffer sizes. Note: `causal_attn` is a graph reuse key (`llm_graph_params` via `cparams`), so a new graph is built regardless of `sched_need_reserve`, so this doesn't change the graph rebuilding behaviour. llama-server with gemma-4-26B-A4B Q4_0 + BF16 mmpro

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11254): ggml : collect all input tensors into graph_inputs (#29634) graph_inputs was populated while splitting the graph, so it only
contained the inputs that are used as srcs of some node. With pipeline
parallelism (n_copies > 1), each graph input contributes n_copies leafs
to graph_copy, so switching between batches that consume different
inputs (e.g. token batches that do not use the embeddings input vs
image batches that do) changed the graph composition. This shifted the
input copies in graph_copy, making the backend ids comparison report
spurious changes and forcing the scheduler to re-reserve. The
re-reserve could then record smaller input sizes (e.g. out_ids with
n_outputs = 0) and abort later on a graph with an unchanged size via
GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC. Collect the inputs after the split instead, from all input leafs of the
graph, so that the graph composition depends only on which inputs
exist, not on which inputs are used. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL **Website:**

F16 path is code-complete and builds clean on host + all 4 DSP arch
variants (v73/v75/v79/v81), but has no F16 test-case coverage in
test-backend-ops and is therefore unverified on-device in this change. * hex-ops: align macros * hex-ops: minor formatting --------- Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11282): musa : define __CUDA_ARCH__ for device passes (#29508) The MUSA vendor header never defined __CUDA_ARCH__, so every architecture
test in the shared ggml-cuda sources evaluated to 0. Kernel bodies gated on
the architecture therefore compiled to nothing, for example the q8_0 -> f16
dequantization kernel in convert.cu, whose NO_DEVICE_CODE fallback expands to
an empty body in host code. Report the newest architecture like the HIP backend does and exclude the
NVIDIA-only features explicitly, as they are not usable on MUSA. Define it
for device passes only: CUB uses defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) to detect device
compilation, which is also how nvcc behaves. Drop the now-redundant defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) checks in the architecture
comparisons: __CUDA_ARCH__ is undefined in host passes for CUDA and MUSA, and
HIP defines it for every pass, so both forms select the same branch. **Website:**
- **Attestations:**
- **macOS/iOS:**
- [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/release

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11276): Hexagon f16 activation ops (#29209) * hexagon: add F16 support for activation ops (SILU/GELU/GELU_QUICK/GEGLU/SWIGLU) Widens ggml_hexagon_supported_activations() to accept F16 (src0/dst/src1
must agree on type), and adds F16 per-thread worker functions in
act-ops.c mirroring the existing F32 workers, backed by new HVX f16
kernels (hvx_sigmoid_f16_aa, hvx_tanh_f16_aa, hvx_mul_mul_f16_aa,
hvx_min_scalar_f16 family). SILU, GELU, GELU_QUICK, GEGLU, and SWIGLU are verified correct on-device
(QRD8850) via test-backend-ops CPU-diffed correctness tests. SWIGLU_OAI's
F16 path is code-complete and builds clean on host + all 4 DSP arch
variants (v73/v75/v79/v81), but has no F16 test-case coverage in
test-backend-ops and is therefore unverified on-device in this change. * hex-ops: align macros * hex-ops: minor formatting --------- Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky **Website:**
- **Attestations:**
- **macOS/iOS:**
- [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11275): gguf : reject tensor size that wraps after padding (#26979) GGML_PAD(nbytes, alignment) wraps to 0 when nbytes is within
(alignment - 1) of SIZE_MAX, which silently bypassed the size
overflow guard in gguf_init_from_reader. Reject the tensor before
padding when nbytes + (alignment - 1) would overflow. Adds a test-gguf handcrafted case (F32, ne = [4, 2^30-1, 2^30+1, 1])
whose ggml_nbytes = 2^64 - 16 lands in the wrap window. Fails on
master, passes with the guard. **Website:**

that fans the embedding out to the hc streams) was first reached through layer 0's
PLE path, after that gather. ggml_backend_sched_split_graph pass 2 expands a device
assignment upwards only until it meets a CPU node, so the REPEAT stayed on the CPU
and the later reshape of hc_init inside the meta split viewed a host-resident node. Expanding hc_init right after it is built puts the REPEAT directly before the first
device node, where pass 2 assigns it; the embedding reshape stays in the CPU split

fills the whole cache: n_ctx tokens complete exactly n_ctx/kpool pools, so
the +1 pads new_pool_idxs/new_pool_rep one entry past n_pool_real. Graph
reserve only covers n_pool_real entries, so the first full-context decode
builds bigger tensors than reserved and ggml-alloc demands a graph
reallocation (abort under GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1). Clamp the bound to n_pool_real: a ubatch can never mark more pools than

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11339): llama : clamp kpool re-pool bound to existing pools (#29805) * tests : simplify function signature * llama : clamp kpool re-pool bound to existing pools The n_tokens/kpool + n_seqs_unq bound on n_new_g overshoots when a batch
fills the whole cache: n_ctx tokens complete exactly n_ctx/kpool pools, so
the +1 pads new_pool_idxs/new_pool_rep one entry past n_pool_real. Graph
reserve only covers n_pool_real entries, so the first full-context decode
builds bigger tensors than reserved and ggml-alloc demands a graph
reallocation (abort under GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1). Clamp the bound to n_pool_real: a ubatch can never mark more pools than
the cache holds, and reserve's n_pool_max already covers that. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * cont : cap to n_pool_max **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11339): llama : clamp kpool re-pool bound to existing pools (#29805) * tests : simplify function signature * llama : clamp kpool re-pool bound to existing pools The n_tokens/kpool + n_seqs_unq bound on n_new_g overshoots when a batch
fills the whole cache: n_ctx tokens complete exactly n_ctx/kpool pools, so
the +1 pads new_pool_idxs/new_pool_rep one entry past n_pool_real. Graph
reserve only covers n_pool_real entries, so the first full-context decode
builds bigger tensors than reserved and ggml-alloc demands a graph
reallocation (abort under GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1). Clamp the bound to n_pool_real: a ubatch can never mark more pools than
the cache holds, and reserve's n_pool_max already covers that. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD * cont : cap to n_pool_max **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11366): ggml-quants : avoid invalid rounding in qkx3 scale search (#29817) * ggml-quants : avoid invalid rounding in qkx3 scale search The imatrix scale search can produce an infinite, NaN, or otherwise out-of-range value when the fitted minimum collapses to the maximum or makes the range extremely small. That value is then passed to nearest_int and can trip its assertion in Debug builds. Clamp the quantization level to [0, nmax] before rounding so valid in-range values behave the same as before while invalid scale-search results no longer reach nearest_int. Add regression coverage for degenerate imatrix groups across q2_K, q4_K, q5_K, q4_1, and q5_1. Fixes #29804. Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 * tests: print degenerate imatrix quant types **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11365): ggml-cpu : fix soft_max_back wrong output when dst aliases src1 (#27096) * ggml-cpu : fix soft_max_back wrong output when dst aliases src1 GGML_OP_SOFT_MAX_BACK is listed in ggml_op_can_inplace, so the graph
allocator may assign dst to alias either src0 (dy) or src1 (y). The result was built in several steps: ggml_vec_cpy_f32 (nc, dx, dy); ggml_vec_acc1_f32 (nc, dx, -dot_y_dy); ggml_vec_mul_f32 (nc, dx, dx, y); ggml_vec_scale_f32(nc, dx, scale); When dst aliases src1, the first step overwrites y and the third step
then reads the overwritten values, so the output is silently wrong.
Aliasing dst with src0 is unaffected. The CUDA kernel completes its
reduction before writing and is already safe. Replace the sequence with a single fused loop that reads both sources
before writing, which is correct under either aliasing. Add a regression test that marks dy as a graph output so the allocator
is forced to alias dst with y, asserts that the alias actually
happened, and compares against values

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11375): graph: gather the recurrent states once so the reserve covers every split (#29856) build_rs gathered the extra states (n_rs - n_seqs rows) with their own
get_rows. The worst-case reserve has n_rs == n_seqs, so that node was
sized at zero rows, and any ubatch whose cells are not contiguous forced
a graph reallocation at an unchanged node count, which aborts under
GGML_SCHED_NO_REALLOC. A single get_rows now gathers the n_rs states: the ubatch states and the
extra states are views of it, and its size only depends on n_rs, which
the reserve already sets to the maximum. A custom getter (mamba ssm_scan)
gathers from the second state, so a single sequence ubatch copies no
state. The views are built once per graph in the input to keep the host
overhead of the graph unchanged. **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11366): ggml-quants : avoid invalid rounding in qkx3 scale search (#29817) * ggml-quants : avoid invalid rounding in qkx3 scale search The imatrix scale search can produce an infinite, NaN, or otherwise out-of-range value when the fitted minimum collapses to the maximum or makes the range extremely small. That value is then passed to nearest_int and can trip its assertion in Debug builds. Clamp the quantization level to [0, nmax] before rounding so valid in-range values behave the same as before while invalid scale-search results no longer reach nearest_int. BLOCK_SIZE chunks, with a workgroup scan per chunk. For decode that is
one workgroup doing KV/1024 barrier-bound iterations, so at 128k cells
it cost more than the sparse attention it feeds. Split the row into contiguous segments instead: one per subgroup with
ballot counting over coalesced loads, or one per thread without
subgroups. A single scan over the segment counts then gives each

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11412): llama : fix unexpected graph reallocation in the k-pool models (#29958) * llama : fix unexpected graph reallocation in the k-pool models Both k-pool models built a graph shape that depends on state the
full-context reserve cannot know: - qwen4exp branched on inp->cache_safe, which turns false as soon as llama_memory_seq_cp shares cells (e.g. batched-bench -pps): the QSA layers swapped scatter+gather for fill+concat and dropped the new_pool_rep leaf, so the decode graph had 12 fewer nodes than the reserved one
- glm5-next branched on gather = n_tokens n_sel, so the TG decode built the gather shape (7564 nodes) while the last reserve, the PP one, had the dense shape (7762 nodes) Either mismatch forces a decode-time re-reserve that drops the
worst-case sizing and bakes in the current state, so the next state
growth (n_pool, n_kv, n_new) needs more room at an unchanged graph size
and aborts under GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1. Reproduce with, e.g.: GGML_SCHED_DEBUG_REALLOC=1 ./bin/llama-batch

- wire both into forward_mul_mat and the repack factory for Q8_0
- docs: mark Q8_0 as supported on X60 Correctness was checked against a quant-exact integer reference for
K = 32 up to 4096, with a max r

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11436): ggml-openvino: fix CI tests; fix GPU regressions. (#30037) * ggml-openvino: skip unselected graph branches and support DUP Upstream #29622 adds a mixed token/embd branch to every input
embedding graph through ggml_build_forward_select(). Its nodes are
not flagged for compute, but the backend translated them anyway,
and the DUP in that branch was unsupported, so the scheduler split
the graph and passed the embeddings across the split with a fixed
token count. The first single-token decode then failed
(test-thread-safety on CPU and GPU). Build the OV model from the compute nodes only, and translate a
same-type contiguous DUP like CONT so the graph stays on one backend. * ggml-openvino: make inp_scale_rows token dim dynamic #29622 also moves the per-token embedding scale (gemma3, gemma3n,
gemma4) into a new [1, n_tokens] input. Give it a dynamic token dim
and pad it per chunk on the static (NPU) path. * ggml-openvino: skip GPU MUL_MAT op tests with unbound Q4_1/Q4_K weights Op tests build

read the full KV cache (all n_kv_heads), negating the memory
bandwidth benefit of multicore on flash_attn. Change both HMX and HVX flash_attn kernels to partition by KV heads
when n_kv_heads is divisible by n_cores: core i processes heads
[i*n_kv_heads/N, (i+1)*n_kv_heads/N) exclusively, reading only its
head shard of the KV cache. Falls back to the original token-block
split when n_kv_heads % n_cores != 0 (e.g. Gemma-4 with 2 KV heads
on 4 cores). Controlled by GGML_HEXAGON_FA_HEAD_SPLIT (default 1 = on).

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11436): ggml-openvino: fix CI tests; fix GPU regressions. (#30037) * ggml-openvino: skip unselected graph branches and support DUP Upstream #29622 adds a mixed token/embd branch to every input
embedding graph through ggml_build_forward_select(). Its nodes are
not flagged for compute, but the backend translated them anyway,
and the DUP in that branch was unsupported, so the scheduler split
the graph and passed the embeddings across the split with a fixed
token count. The first single-token decode then failed
(test-thread-safety on CPU and GPU). Build the OV model from the compute nodes only, and translate a
same-type contiguous DUP like CONT so the graph stays on one backend. * ggml-openvino: make inp_scale_rows token dim dynamic #29622 also moves the per-token embedding scale (gemma3, gemma3n,
gemma4) into a new [1, n_tokens] input. Give it a dynamic token dim
and pad it per chunk on the static (NPU) path. * ggml-openvino: skip GPU MUL_MAT op tests with unbound Q4_1/Q4_K weights Op tests build

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11463): sycl: accelerate GLM MLA prefill with MKL flash attention (#29171) * sycl: accelerate GLM MLA prefill with MKL flash attention GLM-4.7 Flash uses an MLA shape with 576-wide Q/K heads, a 512-wide
V head, GQA 20, and F16 KV. The SYCL dispatcher rejects this shape
because the normal MKL flash-attention gate requires matching K/V
widths and caps the head dimension at 512, so prompt processing falls
back to the substantially slower TILE kernel. Admit only the validated 576/576/512, GQA-20 F16 shape to the existing
MKL pipeline. Keep all other mismatched K/V shapes on their current
fallback paths. Handle GLM's V cache as a narrower strided view of K rows. Select the
strided F16 descriptor when row stride is padded, and alias K/V
dequantization buffers only when their logical widths match. Restrict
the stride exception to a real V view sharing K's row stride. Add the exact 576/512, GQA-20 prompt-path backend test. On an Intel Arc Pro B70 at master e613ef2, pp8192 improves from
432.80 to 1292.

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11474): feat: add GLM5Next MTP, optimize (#29928) * llama : add GLM5-Next NextN (MTP) graph Build the GLM5-Next multi-token-prediction head as graph_mtp: the NextN block

shared lm_head, reusing the trunk's builders through the no_build tag ctor.

no recurrent layers, which is what the MTP draft context needs. Assisted-by: Claude * llama : glm5-next: skip dead compute in headless NextN forwards A NextN forward with no output rows (the MTP catch-up and the draft-context

the MLA latent, indexer key|gate and pooled-key writes and drops the query
path, the indexer selection, the attention body, the FFN and the LM head. The
4-token catch-up falls from 6.9 ms to 0.33 ms of kernels; the greedy output
hashes and the draft acceptance are unchanged. Assisted-by: Claude * llama

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11509): CUDA: fix CCCL version guard breaking on major version rollover (#29453) * CUDA: fix CCCL version guard breaking on major version rollover The guard compared the major and minor components independently: CCCL_MAJOR_VERSION >= 3 && CCCL_MINOR_VERSION >= 1 Minor resets to 0 whenever a new major series is cut, so on CCCL 4.x
this evaluates as 4 >= 3 && 0 >= 1, i.e. false. STRIDED_ITERATOR_AVAILABLE
stops being defined and argsort silently falls back to the
init_offsets path. Nothing warns and the build still succeeds, so the
regression is a quiet performance loss rather than a compile error. CCCL already exposes the version as a single packed integer in
MMMmmmpp form, which is what its own version header uses: CCCL_VERSION = MAJOR * 1000000 + MINOR * 1000 + PATCH so 3.4.3 is 3004003 and ">= 3.1" is a plain ">= 3001000". One
comparison, with no component arithmetic left to get wrong. Checked against a hand-written "version >= 3.1" reference over 2.9.9,
3.0.0, 3.1.0, 3.1.99, 3.2.0, 3.4.3, 3

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11505): vulkan : fix TOP_K for +inf/NaN inputs and k = 1 on negative values (#30107) The bucket search in topk_nary_search.comp started from the range
[0, 0xFF800000), which ends just below the ordered-uint mapping of +inf,
so +inf and NaN were never counted. A workgroup block with fewer than k
countable values left the ballot empty and the shader read uninitialized
shared state (hang/device lost on NVIDIA, wrong indices on AMD), and a few
+inf in a block were selected without being counted, dropping real top
values. Map NaN to -inf on input, start from [0, 0xFFFFFFFF) so every value is
counted, and clamp the top bucket's end (2^32) instead of wrapping to 0. The k = 1 path compared float bits as signed integers, which orders
negative values backwards; compare floats instead. Add test_top_k_inf to test-backend-ops: negative values, fewer than k
+inf and many -inf, for k = 1, 10, 40. Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11516): hexagon: fix IM2COL patch-embed DMA ring overflow (#30189) * hexagon: fix IM2COL patch-embed DMA ring overflow The exact-tiling (stride == kernel, no pad/dilation) IM2COL DMA kernel
issues IC*KH DDR->VTCM descriptors per output row without checking the
return value of dma_queue_push(), and then pops IC*KH times. The per-thread
DMA ring holds 256 entries and a push into a full ring returns false
and drops the transfer, so for IC*KH > 255 the remaining rows of the
VTCM staging buffer were never written and stale data (often NaN/inf)
leaked into the output. Solution is to retire the oldest descriptor when the ring is full, just as the blocked
kernel in the same file already does, and wait with dma_queue_flush(). For testing, added exact-tiling test cases with IC*KH > 256 (2D 1x1, 2D 2x2 patch
embed and 1D, F16 and F32 dst), which fail on HTP without this fix. * Apply suggestion from @max-krasnyansky --------- Co-authored-by: Max Krasnyansky **Website:**
- **Attestations:**
- **macOS/iOS:*

gated on GGML_CUDA_TOPK_RADIX_MIN_ROWS. On qwen4exp at 34,816 tokens this cuts
top-k from 1,671,253 launches / 5,761.8 ms to 2,329 / 941.8 ms. * CUDA: select the TOP_K implementation by shape Replace the nrows/ncols special case with the decision boundary from #28547
(as implemented in #29278): bitonic for short rows, radix select for several
long rows, and DeviceTopK or CUB argsort for a single long row. The
thresholds stay overridable at build time. Two refinements on top of that boundary:
- bitonic stays in use for rows up to a padded 1024 while the rows fit in one wave of blocks (nrows <= number of SMs); radix select pays a fixed cost of about a dozen launches that only amortizes over more rows
- with DeviceTopK available, it handles up to two rows Radix select now processes rows in chunks so its scratch memory stays b

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11528): meta : handle host views (#30217) * meta : handle views of tensors allocated on the host A view shares the memory of its view_src, so ggml-alloc never allocates a view in
the buffer of the split it lands in - the scheduler copies the source into the
split and the ops that use the view read that copy. The view node itself is a noop
and does not need a split of its own, but the meta backend asserted when one was
left inside a meta split: - ggml_backend_meta_get_split_state() dereferenced tensor->buffer->context - the graph rebuild mapped every node with ggml_backend_meta_buffer_simple_tensor() Accept such nodes when they are views of host tensors, which also generalizes the
previous s_copy_main workaround. This fixes the assert hit by KV cache views when

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11557): rpc : turn GGML_RPC_DEBUG into a verbosity level and add logs (#29544) * rpc : turn GGML_RPC_DEBUG into a verbosity level and add logs GGML_RPC_DEBUG is now parsed as a number: 0/unset disables debug logs,
1-3 emit increasingly detailed output (events, per-command trace,
transport detail). Non-numeric values fall back to 1. The duplicated env/macro blocks in ggml-rpc.cpp and transport.cpp are
replaced by a shared log.h, which becomes the single choke point for
all logging of the RPC backend: LOG_ERROR/LOG_WARN/LOG_INFO for
unconditional severity logs and LOG_DBG/LOG_DBG2/LOG_DBG3 for the
verbosity-gated ones. The transport files no longer need ggml-impl.h,
and the server banner now also goes through the ggml logger (stderr). Missing logs are added on both the client (handshake, buffer ops,
tensor transfers, graph computes, cache decisions) and the server
(per-command dispatch, graph nodes), including the negotiated
transport via the new socket_t::transport_name(). Assisted-by: pi:llama

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11557): rpc : turn GGML_RPC_DEBUG into a verbosity level and add logs (#29544) * rpc : turn GGML_RPC_DEBUG into a verbosity level and add logs GGML_RPC_DEBUG is now parsed as a number: 0/unset disables debug logs,
1-3 emit increasingly detailed output (events, per-command trace,
transport detail). Non-numeric values fall back to 1. The duplicated env/macro blocks in ggml-rpc.cpp and transport.cpp are
replaced by a shared log.h, which becomes the single choke point for
all logging of the RPC backend: LOG_ERROR/LOG_WARN/LOG_INFO for
unconditional severity logs and LOG_DBG/LOG_DBG2/LOG_DBG3 for the
verbosity-gated ones. The transport files no longer need ggml-impl.h,
and the server banner now also goes through the ggml logger (stderr). Missing logs are added on both the client (handshake, buffer ops,
tensor transfers, graph computes, cache decisions) and the server
(per-command dispatch, graph nodes), including the negotiated
transport via the new socket_t::transport_name(). Assisted-by: pi:llama

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11569): metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids (#30373) * metal : fix mul_mat_id limits and kernel name * metal : fix mul_mat_id with duplicate ids kernel_mul_mm_id_map0 assumed at most one match per token and a fixed
capacity of ne21 entries per expert, which produced wrong or dropped
output rows and could overflow into the slice of the next expert when
the ids contain duplicates. build a compact per-expert list of the (token, slot) entries instead: - pass 1 counts the entries of every expert, thread 0 computes the offsets of the expert slices (tpe now holds [base, count])
- pass 2 writes the entries with one unconditional store per token (conditional stores of divergent lanes are very slow), the dummy value of the tokens without a match lands on a padding slot of the slice that is never read - duplicates are handled by a rare branch
- kernel_mul_mm_id reads the base/count of its expert and loops over the entry tiles that do not fit into the grid The ids buffer is sized as ne20*ne21 + ne02

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11567): llama : report compute graph reallocations during inference (#30329) Add an optional ggml_backend_sched_realloc_callback that user code registers with
ggml_backend_sched_set_realloc_callback to be notified when the buffers reserved for a
graph are not sufficient and have to be reserved again. The callback reports whether the
backend assignments and the graph size changed since the previous scheduling. llama_context registers the callback when creating the scheduler (wrapped into the new
llama_context::sched_new helper) and treats the reallocations that follow a change of the
backend assignments as expected, counting the rest by graph size - unchanged or changed
from the previously scheduled graph. Both counters are reported on one line in the perf
stats. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **Website:**
- **Attestations:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11576): graph: pad the KV dimension of the no-cache attention to 256 (#30416) The no-cache path builds a [n_tokens, n_tokens] mask and passes K and V
unpadded, so FLASH_ATTN_EXT sees K->ne[1] == n_tokens. The CUDA kernels
for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls
back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token)
disables flash attention for such models. Pad the mask like llama_kv_cache::get_n_kv and pad K and V with zeros up
to the KV dimension of the mask. clef builds its own causal mask and
pads it the same way. **Website:**

unpadded, so FLASH_ATTN_EXT sees K->ne[1] == n_tokens. The CUDA kernels
for head size 512 require a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE, so the op falls
back to the CPU for most lengths, and the -fa auto probe (1 token)
disables flash attention for such models. Pad the mask like llama_kv_cache::get_n_kv and pad K and V with zeros up
to the KV dimension of the mask. clef builds its own causal mask and
pads it the same way. **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11642): server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498) * server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts,
while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank,
embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit
without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered
again at every task start. Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable
and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot
restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both
save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for
completion tasks. * server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new
tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or
without a unified KV cache. * server: restore any reusing task from the prompt

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11636): sycl: IQ3 code reorder (#29107) * sycl: persistent IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS weight reorder for SYCL decode and prefill Add persistent reordered weight layouts for IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS. Weights
are reordered once at load time; the reordered MMVQ dot products then
walk dense super-blocks with dp4a and SWAR sign expansion instead of
gathering bits from the interleaved standard layout. Reorder-aware
dequantization feeds the batched prefill GEMMs so prompt processing
sees the same benefit. Also harden the oneDNN build check: a missing DNNL package or a
CPU-only DNNL build now fails at configure time instead of silently
producing a degraded backend. Measured on Intel Arc Pro B70 with Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S (MTP),
-ngl 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -fa on: tg256 @ 0 ctx 12.92 -> 23.54 tok/s (+82%)
tg256 @ 9,216 12.33 -> 21.69 tok/s (+76%)
tg256 @ 64,000 9.76 -> 14.91 tok/s (+53%)
pp8192 833.9 -> 833.6 tok/s (flat) Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M / Q3_K_M are unchanged within noise (largest delta
-0.5% pp, tg flat), so standar

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11630): ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input (#28738) * ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product
sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N].
The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires:
no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out
interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe
the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never
hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call. Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path
keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph
and pay for no extra copy. tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N
single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same
input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and
all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1 pass either way

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11642): server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498) * server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts,
while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank,
embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit
without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered
again at every task start. Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable
and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot
restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both
save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for
completion tasks. * server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new
tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or
without a unified KV cache. * server: restore any reusing task from the prompt

layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE.

markers that can be mapped to their respective logits for the output

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11703): hexagon: vectorize softplus with HVX (#30435) softplus_f32 and tile_softplus_f32 ran a scalar logf(1.0f + expf(x)) loop.
Replace both with a shared hvx_softplus_f32_aa() helper built from the
backend's existing hvx_vec_exp_f32 / hvx_vec_log_f32 primitives, so no new
numerical approximation is introduced. hvx_vec_exp_f32 clamps its input to (-88, 88) before exponentiating, so a
naive log(1 + exp(x)) composition would saturate to ~88.72 for large x
instead of returning x. The Q6_V_vmux_QVV select keeps the scalar
reference's x > 20 guard (ggml_compute_softplus_f32 in ggml-impl.h),
which is what makes the vector path match the CPU result. Assisted-by: Claude **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11712): tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about
six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a
threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state
keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a
different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model
carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate
holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one
raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then
scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary
factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test
ran on were not a Muse Spark. P

layer. The sliding layers rotate with NeoX RoPE, the full layers are NoPE.

sigmoid of the unbiased logits, without renorm. The converter reuses AfmoeModel for the per-expert checkpoint layout and
the expert selection bias, and writes the shared expert and the per layer
sliding window pattern. The released FP8 checkpoint needs no special code,
it goes through the generic weight_s

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11712): tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table (#30674) * tests: give the random model generator a per-tensor filler table Muse Spark makes test-llama-context fail on state_load, cp_h and cp_d on about
six percent of the random seeds, with an NMSE of 1.0e-05 to 1.4e-05 against a
threshold of 1.0e-05. The sliding window is what exposes it: a restored state
keeps the window alone, so the attention of an SWA layer reduces over a
different cell layout and the continuation is not bit exact. Every SWA model
carries that, at 1e-08. Muse Spark carried it at 1e-05. The generator is what turns 1e-08 into 1e-05. A norm preserving residual gate
holds alpha^2 + beta^2 == 1 and the conversion resolves both weights from one
raw weight, while the generator draws every tensor on its own. The pair then
scaled the stream and the branch independently, the stream lost an arbitrary
factor at each layer, and the model became an amplifier. The weights the test
ran on were not a Muse Spark. P

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11752): tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise (#30818) * tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise The router scores are in the range [0, 1), so a random draw can leave the
last expert (or expert group) still selected and the first one dropped tied
within the noise between the backends. They then route a token to different
experts and the logits differ by 4e-3 instead of the usual 5e-7. Beam is the only arch here with a real top-k (8 experts, 2 used) and a group
top-k (4 groups, 2 used), so it is the only one that hits this: 2 of 20 seeds
failed on an M2 Ultra, the other MoE archs select 2 of 2 and cannot tie. Fill the selection bias with a ramp of step 2 to give every expert a score
range of its own, which turns the top-k into a function of the expert index
alone. The bias affects only the selection, the weights still come from the
unbiased probs, so the MoE output keeps its magnitude. Beam now matches the
CPU reference within 4e-7 for all

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11752): tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise (#30818) * tests : make MoE router selection independent of the backend noise The router scores are in the range [0, 1), so a random draw can leave the
last expert (or expert group) still selected and the first one dropped tied
within the noise between the backends. They then route a token to different
experts and the logits differ by 4e-3 instead of the usual 5e-7. Beam is the only arch here with a real top-k (8 experts, 2 used) and a group
top-k (4 groups, 2 used), so it is the only one that hits this: 2 of 20 seeds
failed on an M2 Ultra, the other MoE archs select 2 of 2 and cannot tie. Fill the selection bias with a ramp of step 2 to give every expert a score
range of its own, which turns the top-k into a function of the expert index
alone. The bias affects only the selection, the weights still come from the
unbiased probs, so the MoE output keeps its magnitude. Beam now matches the
CPU reference within 4e-7 for all

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11774): mtmd : lfm2 tiles and layout match transformers (#30261) * mtmd : lfm2 tiles stretch the image to the grid Lfm2VlImageProcessor.crop_image_to_patches resizes the image straight to
(512 * rows, 512 * cols) before it cuts the tiles. llama.cpp kept the aspect
ratio and added black bars for LFM2 (only d1-omni stretched), so the tiles of
d1-3B and every LFM2-VL / LFM2.5-VL model differed from transformers unless
the image had the aspect ratio of the grid. With PAD_NONE the tiles are the
same as in transformers. * mtmd : lfm2 layout with Python rounding in double precision Lfm2VlImageProcessor.smart_resize rounds with Python's round (half to even)
and computes beta and the tile grid aspect ratio in double. llama.cpp used
std::round and float, so 31926 of the 16.7M sizes in [1,4096]^2 got another
thumbnail size or grid than transformers (and d1-omni vision.py), e.g.
400x600 -> 416x608 instead of 384x608 and 720x1600 -> 2x5 tiles instead of
2x4. The lfm2 smart resize and grid choice now follow

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11815): sycl: fix CONV_2D wrong results for non-contiguous input (#30363) * sycl: fix CONV_2D wrong results for non-contiguous input The kernel indexes the `input` as a contiguous [W, H, C, N] tensor, but
supports_op claimed the op for any layout. A non-contiguous (e.g. `CWHN`
permuted) input was read with the wrong element offsets, silently
producing wrong results. Gate the CONV_2D op on `input` and `kernel` contiguity, matching the
CUDA backend contract, and assert input contiguity in the op. `test-backend-ops -b SYCL0 -o CONV_2D`: goes from 16 failures to 0,
none. ```text 2006/2006 tests passed Backend SYCL0: OK
Backend 2/2: CPU Skipping
2/2 backends passed
OK
``` Assisted-by: pi (unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:Q4_K_M via llama.cpp) * sycl : CONV_2D cwhn=1 support Make the SYCL backend compute `GGML_OP_CONV_2D` correctly for `cwhn=1` (CWHN
channel-order) inputs and kernels, so the previously failing test-
backend-ops CONV_2D cases pass on SYCL instead of being skipped or
miscomputed. - Implement

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11822): model : fix qwen4exp layer inputs for DFlash drafters (#30927) qwen4exp published the hc-wide residual [n_embd, hc, n_tokens] as
t_layer_inp, but the drafter reads layer inputs as [n_embd, n_tokens]
rows: llama_context sizes each embd_layer_inp buffer as n_embd * n_batch
and the DFlash encoder input is n_extract * n_embd wide. Evaluating a
DFlash draft over a qwen4exp target therefore aborts on the first request
in llama_context::extract_layer_inputs. Collapse the streams with a plain mean before exposing them, as deepseek4
already does for its hyper-connection residual, and build the mean only
for the layers a drafter actually requested. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) **Website:**

proxy: audio appended while the tail drains leaks into the committed

flushed audio (mtmd_audio_stream_get_n_rows_flushed), next to the rows
produced so far (mtmd_audio_stream_get_n_rows). The slot keeps a FIFO

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11822): model : fix qwen4exp layer inputs for DFlash drafters (#30927) qwen4exp published the hc-wide residual [n_embd, hc, n_tokens] as
t_layer_inp, but the drafter reads layer inputs as [n_embd, n_tokens]
rows: llama_context sizes each embd_layer_inp buffer as n_embd * n_batch
and the DFlash encoder input is n_extract * n_embd wide. Evaluating a
DFlash draft over a qwen4exp target therefore aborts on the first request
in llama_context::extract_layer_inputs. Collapse the streams with a plain mean before exposing them, as deepseek4
already does for its hyper-connection residual, and build the mean only
for the layers a drafter actually requested. Assisted-by: pi:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) **Website:**

the values of the d1-omni and LFM2.5-VL crops. RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR_TORCH rounds the weights of the Pillow port to that

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11847): hip: fix bf16 WMMA operand vector type for gfx11/gfx12 (#30885) The __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32 (and _gfx12) builtins
take their A/B operands as vectors of short (_ExtVector /
_ExtVector ), not __bf16. Declaring the fragments as
ext_vector_type(N) __bf16 fails to compile: error: cannot initialize a parameter of type 'short __attribute__((ext_vector_type(16)))' with an lvalue of type 'const bf16x16_t' (vector of 16 '__bf16' values) short and __bf16 are both 16-bit and the value is only ever passed to
the builtin via reinterpret_cast over raw bytes, so changing the element
type is bit-identical. The operand type has been short since the builtin
was introduced, so this works across LLVM/ROCm versions without a
version gate. Fixes HIP builds for RDNA3 (gfx1150/1151) and RDNA4
(gfx1200/1201). Signed-off-by: Pablo Cholaky **Website:**
- **Attestations:**
- **macOS/iOS:**
- [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11847/llama-b1184

weights are int16 with as many fractional bits as the largest weight allows,
where Pillow uses 22 bits. The Pillow port was 1-2 levels off on about 1% of
the values of the d1-omni and LFM2.5-VL crops. RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR_TORCH rounds the weights of the Pillow port to that
precision and scales them back to 22 bits, which gives the output of
torchvision with the same passes, and "bilinear" maps to it for LFM2 and
d1-omni. Other models keep the Pillow algorithms. * mtmd : lfm2 bicubic resize matches torchvision Lfm2VlImageProcessor resizes with torchvision for the bicubic checkpoints too

weights o

the values of the d1-omni and LFM2.5-VL crops. RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR_TORCH rounds the weights of the Pillow port to that

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11847): hip: fix bf16 WMMA operand vector type for gfx11/gfx12 (#30885) The __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32 (and _gfx12) builtins
take their A/B operands as vectors of short (_ExtVector /
_ExtVector ), not __bf16. Declaring the fragments as
ext_vector_type(N) __bf16 fails to compile: error: cannot initialize a parameter of type 'short __attribute__((ext_vector_type(16)))' with an lvalue of type 'const bf16x16_t' (vector of 16 '__bf16' values) short and __bf16 are both 16-bit and the value is only ever passed to
the builtin via reinterpret_cast over raw bytes, so changing the element
type is bit-identical. The operand type has been short since the builtin
was introduced, so this works across LLVM/ROCm versions without a
version gate. Fixes HIP builds for RDNA3 (gfx1150/1151) and RDNA4
(gfx1200/1201). Signed-off-by: Pablo Cholaky **Website:**
- **Attestations:**
- **macOS/iOS:**
- [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11847/llama-b1184

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11861): minimax-m3 : forward quant scales to the graph (fixes #31063) (#31097) The generic scale pass in llama-model.cpp loads the per-expert
NVFP4 scale2 tensors (ffn_{up,gate,down}_exps_s) and the per-tensor
MXFP8 scales for the dense FFN and the shared expert, but
minimax-m3.cpp never forwarded any of them to the graph. build_moe_ffn() defaults these to nullptr, so build_lora_mm_id()
skipped its w_s branch entirely and the routed-expert weights came
out global_scale times too large, swamping the residual (reported
G ~= 15123 for M3.1 Flash) and producing token soup. Forward all scale tensors at the three call sites, matching the
pattern used by flint and the other NVFP4-capable MoE models. Co-authored-by: origin-labs-ai **Website:**
- **Attestations:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11883): llama-quant : fix 4D tensor quantization using ggml_nrows() and name-based expert detection (#30820) * llama-quant : fix quantizing 4D tensors nrows_total was ne[1]*ne[2], so for a 4D tensor only the first ne[2]
slices were quantized and the rest of the rows were dropped. Use
ggml_nrows(tensor) to count all rows, including ne[3]. Fixes #29916 * llama-quant : detect expert tensors by name and fix imatrix size for 4D tensors The MXFP4_MOE path used ne[2] > 1 to detect MoE expert tensors. This is
wrong for non-expert tensors with 3 or more dims, e.g. MLA projections
(BailingMoE3) and 4D conv kernels. Use the tensor name instead: all
tensors used by GGML_OP_MUL_MAT_ID are named *_exps or *_chexps. This
also removes the BailingMoE3 special case. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the
expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how
the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5 **Websi

from the HF API, chosen to cover every file naming pattern found across
1237 GGUF repos of the major publishers and pruned to whole quant groups.
Each repo pins its resolved plans and its cache listing. The expectations follow what each file really is per its GGUF header,
not what the current resolver picks, so a mismatch is a resolution bug.
Mismatches are collected and reported together before the test fails. * tests: leave the listing unchecked on paths the filesystem refuses Some real split names (DevQuasar's Model.Q2_K.gguf-00001-of-00012.gguf

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11928): model: Add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev (#30980) * model : add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev support The model is a Qwen3.5-VL trunk with a value head read at the last token: it
scores an OCR text against an image rendered from it, it does not generate. Add the openbmb-minicpm-ocr-jev decision type, served by POST /v1/systemone.
The class scores are the pooled output of the sequence, read with last pooling,
so the conversion turns score.weight into cls.output and sets
embedding_length_out. The checkpoint has no LM head, so text generation is
rejected instead of using the output weights duplicated from the token
embeddings. The task is fixed, so its prompt is entirely in the systemone template, the
same way h2o-lightning keeps its default there. The processor of the checkpoint
allows up to 16384 merged tokens per image, more than the Qwen-VL default of
mtmd, so the mmproj keeps the image budget of the preprocessor config. The
checkpoint declares MiniCPMOCRForSequenceClassification in its config.json, as
other mod

A batch of new architectures landed: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, SenseNova U1, Beam, Kolibri-1, Flint, Muse Spark, Granite Switch Decision, plus decision/embedding models from LiquidAI, Baidu and NVIDIA. The core got sparse-attention (QSA/DSA) reworked onto a fused masking op, a 50/50 SLRU cache for host-resident MoE experts, and cleaner `no_alloc` memory handling; the server got router memory-management and tool-calling improvements; the UI can now browse and download models straight from HF Hub, search conversations and compact them. Finally, `ggml` was bumped to v0.28.0, bringing `GGML_OP_TOP_K_MASK`, `-1` expert-index semantics and large backend performance work (CUDA chunked graph launches, SYCL graph replay, OpenCL Q2_K/Q3_K, Hexagon HTP

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11977): ggml-openvino: slice view inputs of SCALE (#31334) SCALE now accepts a src0 view with arbitrary row strides. translate_scale
used the raw input, and on the dynamic path a VIEW translates to its whole
source tensor, so a strided view input scaled the entire source. The model
output then had the source's size, and copying it back overran the result
buffer, which crashes test-backend-ops on the SCALE view cases. Slice the input with process_view_input_new, as the other translators do.
Reject an in-place SCALE on a non-contiguous view: its result is copied
back densely and would land in the wrong elements. **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11985): metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec, full threadgroups for unary/binary/GLU (#31075) * metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec kernel Decode the fp4 values with the fp16 bit trick instead of a threadgroup lookup table, and load the packed nibbles as aligned 32-bit words. The kernel no longer uses threadgroup memory. * metal : launch contiguous unary and binary ops with full threadgroups The contiguous unary path and the row-broadcast binary path used one thread per threadgroup. Use up to 256 threads per threadgroup and bound-check the tail. * metal : split GLU rows across threadgroups A GLU row ran on one threadgroup, so single-row decode used a single threadgroup for the whole op. Offizielle Release-Notes (b11977): ggml-openvino: slice view inputs of SCALE (#31334) SCALE now accepts a src0 view with arbitrary row strides. translate_scale
used the raw input, and on the dynamic path a VIEW translates to its whole
source tensor, so a strided view input scaled the entire source. The model
output then had the source's size, and copying it back overran the result
buffer, which crashes test-backend-ops on the SCALE view cases. Slice the input with process_view_input_new, as the other translators do.
Reject an in-place SCALE on a non-contiguous view: its result is copied
back densely and would land in the wrong elements. **Website:**

Offizielle Release-Notes (b11985): metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec, full threadgroups for unary/binary/GLU (#31075) * metal : faster MXFP4 mat-vec kernel Decode the fp4 values with the fp16 bit trick instead of a threadgroup lookup table, and load the packed nibbles as aligned 32-bit words. The kernel no longer uses threadgroup memory. * metal : launch contiguous unary and binary ops with full threadgroups The contiguous unary path and the row-broadcast binary path used one thread per threadgroup. Use up to 256 threads per threadgroup and bound-check the tail. * metal : split GLU rows across threadgroups A GLU row ran on one threadgroup, so single-row decode used a single threadgroup for the whole op. Split each row over threadgroups of up to 256 threads. **Website:**

Hinweis: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357. Erforderliche Massnahme: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.
